summary: French designer Coco Chanel rose from a convent orphanage to reinvent women's fashion and Chanel No. 5, while embracing virulent antisemitism, funding a far-right paper and spying for Nazi Germany during the occupation.

evidence.note: Birth in 1883 in a Saumur poorhouse
Convent education instils antisemitism; her later antisemitic outbursts
Capel funds her first business, the hat line, start of main span
Legacy segment: disposable fashion and modern garment workers in Bangladesh
Enters British high society via Vera Bate; decade with the Duke of Westminster
She bankrolls Iribe's relaunch of Le Temoin as a nationalist antisemitic paper
1936 Popular Front strike by about 4,000 of her workers and her resistance
Registered as an Abwehr agent; spying trip to Madrid in 1941
Uses Aryanisation laws to try to seize the perfume firm from the Wertheimers
1943 separate-peace scheme with Vera Bate collapses in Madrid
Arrest after liberation in 1944, release, exile in Switzerland
1954 comeback, death in 1971, 2011 book exposes her Abwehr work

notes: main_span runs from the first boutique (about 1910) to the end of her wartime collaboration in 1945. Switzerland exile and Hollywood stint were brief, so CH and US are left out of the setting. reaches_present rests on the fast-fashion legacy segment and the 2011 revelations with the brand's response.
